steps.what: Draft the impact of proposed regulations

loop.output: claims that cite one clause id and one service id
loop.check: Every claim cites a clause id and a service id that exist
loop.stop: One pass; drop any claim missing either id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a clause matters here is not a keyword match

steps.what: Check each claim against the source rows
Analyze services impacted and sign the note

tasks.design: Proposed texts are stored in {DOCS} with clause id, service id and a short title. A bounded note drafts how those clauses could affect services, and every claim cites a clause id and a service id. The manager checks the citations, signs the impact, and only that note is filed. The note does not change a service on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule changes arrived as long documents in mail, so an impact note could not show which clause it meant.
tasks.enabler_now: A clause id and a service id can be stored together, so a claim without both can be dropped.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a change actually hurts a service is a judgement about this organisation, not a keyword.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the impact and signs it. A draft that invents a clause is rejected.

ambition.what: Review each proposed rule when it is published, not only in a yearly sweep

tasks.altitude: Less time hunting the clause. The judgement stays. The manager can refuse a note whose citations do not match the text.

reach.task: Adjust a service only after the signed impact note
reach.learn: Which clauses are signed as relevant and which were dropped

evidence.claim: Analyzing proposed rules is document work plus a judgement. The meeting share in the prior overstates this task. The time sits on the texts.
Digest [S1] describes policy-library management that classifies and summarises regulatory documents and flags gaps, for a person to approve.
Digest [S2] describes a European governance, risk and compliance register with regulatory monitoring for policy and control tasks. It is not a measured result for this team.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. Each impact claim is checked against the clause and service rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends at a signed impact note. Changing a live service is a later decision.
Input contract: clause id, instrument title, service id, published date, summary already in the text. Producer is the manager from the official text. A claim with no clause id is dropped.
The prior is meeting-heavy. For this task the means are documents. Use the document store's own versions before custom code. The manager still signs.
unknowns: Which official texts are obtained as files rather than as paper.
Who signs an impact note when the manager is away.
research_questions: What share of proposed texts is stored with a clause id?
How often does the manager reject a claim for a bad citation?

already_counted.description: Manager edits claims that cite a weak clause
Citation check stays with the manager

incremental.description: Add service ids when a program starts or stops

approvals.approved_version: impact note signed for this instrument

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes proposed texts stay as unstructured mail, so the draft rarely cites a real clause and the manager still reads by hand. The high case assumes clause rows exist but every impact judgement and the sign-off stay manual. No change to a live service is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Pull lines for programs and equipment
Draft commentary for budgets and services

loop.input: budget lines and the commentary template
loop.output: prose whose numbers equal line amounts
loop.check: Every number in the commentary equals a line amount
loop.stop: One pass; drop any sentence with a number that is not on a line
loop.why_not_simpler: Which line to cut is not a formula

steps.what: Administer budgets in the review meeting
Sign the budgets for support services

tasks.design: Budget lines in {SPREADSHEET} carry line id, program id, equipment flag, amount and period. A bounded commentary in {DOCS} may state only numbers that equal those lines. The manager administers changes in the review, signs one budgets version, and only that version is filed. A later payment is out of scope.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commentary was typed beside figures that had already changed, so a sentence could name a number the sheet no longer held.
tasks.enabler_now: Line id and amount can be read from the sheet, so a sentence can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Which program or equipment line to cut or keep is still a management decision.
tasks.human_edge: The manager administers the budget and signs it. The commentary cannot invent a figure.

ambition.what: Look at budget lines every month, not only when the year-end pack is due

tasks.altitude: Less time retyping figures into prose. The manager still decides the lines and can refuse commentary that does not match them.

reach.task: Post only the signed budget version
reach.learn: Which line amounts are signed and which commentary was dropped

evidence.claim: Administering a program budget is a sheet plus a decision. Commentary is useful only when every number matches a line. The decision is not a formula.
Digest [S7] describes document drafting from approved text where a person still checks. Budget commentary here is checked against the figure rows before it is signed.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends at a signed budget version. Paying an invoice is out of scope.
Input contract: line id, program id, equipment flag, amount, period, owner. Producer is the budget sheet. A sentence whose number is not on a line is dropped.
Meetings are the decision, not the whole task. Time also sits on the spreadsheet and the document. Use the sheet's own totals before custom code.
unknowns: Whether equipment lines use the same sheet as program lines.
Who signs a budget when the manager is away.
research_questions: What share of commentary numbers does not match a line today?
How often is a signed line changed before the next period?

already_counted.description: Manager edits commentary that misses a line
Budget decisions in the review stay with the manager

incremental.description: Add a commentary section when a new program line appears

approvals.approved_version: budget version signed for this period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes budget lines are not stable ids, so commentary is still written by hand. The high case assumes lines are clean but every administered change and the sign-off stay with the manager. Payments are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Draft holding text for media institutions

loop.input: signed fact rows and the holding template
loop.output: text in which each sentence cites a fact id
loop.check: Every sentence cites a fact id on the signed rows
loop.stop: One pass; drop any sentence with no fact id
loop.why_not_simpler: How to answer a live question is not a stored fact

steps.what: Sign the text on behalf of the organizations
Send the signed text to media institutions

tasks.design: A holding text in {DOCS} is drafted only from signed fact rows: fact id, date and the sentence already approved. The manager signs that public text. The meeting with governmental or media institutions stays on the {CALENDAR}. {EMAIL} sends only the signed text.
tasks.previous_blocker: Public lines were drafted in the hour before a call, with no list of which facts had been signed.
tasks.enabler_now: A fact id can mark a sentence the manager has already accepted, so an unsigned fact can be kept out of the text.
tasks.still_hard: What to say to a journalist or an official, in the moment, is still the manager's call.
tasks.human_edge: The manager represents the organization and signs every public sentence before it is sent.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays. The manager can refuse a holding text that uses a fact not on the signed list, and nothing is sent before that signature.

reach.task: Receive only the signed public text
reach.learn: Which sentences are signed and which questions were not answered

evidence.claim: Representing an organisation to government or the media is a meeting. A holding text can be prepared. The conversation cannot.
Digest [S7] describes document drafting from approved text where a person still checks. The holding text uses signed facts and the manager signs again before sending.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. Public text is checked against the fact rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends when the meeting has happened and only the signed text has been sent. A legal dispute is out of scope.
Input contract: fact id, date, approved sentence, audience, matter id. Producer is the manager from facts already signed. A sentence with no fact id is dropped.
The meeting prior fits and is accepted. Use the document store's own template before custom code. The send uses the signed version only.
unknowns: Who may speak to the media when the manager is away.
Which matters need a governmental meeting rather than a written text.
research_questions: What share of holding sentences has a fact id?
How often does the meeting go beyond the signed text?

already_counted.description: Manager edits the holding text before signing
Representation time stays in the meeting

incremental.description: Add fact rows when a matter gains a new signed sentence

approvals.approved_version: public text signed for this matter id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes facts are not stored as rows, so the holding text is still written by hand. The high case assumes the draft is clean but the sign-off, the meeting and any unscripted answer stay with the manager. Representation time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Draft public relations materials from fact rows

loop.input: signed fact rows and the materials template
loop.output: materials in which each line cites a fact id
loop.check: Every public line cites a fact id on the signed rows
loop.stop: One pass; drop any line with no fact id
loop.why_not_simpler: The tone of an appeal is not a stored field

steps.what: Direct fundraising activities for this period
Sign the fundraising materials for release
Send the signed public relations materials

tasks.design: Public relations materials in {DOCS} are drafted from fact rows only: fact id, appeal id and an approved sentence. The manager directs the fundraising activities in person, then signs the materials. {EMAIL} sends only that signed version. An unsigned draft is not released.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appeal text was rewritten from last year's file, and the facts behind a line were not listed.
tasks.enabler_now: A fact id can tie a public sentence to a row the manager has already accepted.
tasks.still_hard: Asking for money, and how to direct the people doing it, is still a human activity.
tasks.human_edge: The manager directs the fundraising and signs the materials. Nothing public goes out on an unsigned draft.

ambition.what: Sign materials before each public push, not in one batch at the end of the appeal

tasks.altitude: The activities stay. The manager spends less time rebuilding old text and can stop a line that has no fact id.

reach.task: Receive only materials the manager has signed
reach.learn: Which appeal version is current and which lines were dropped

evidence.claim: Fundraising is an activity plus materials. The activity stays with people. The materials can be drafted from sentences already approved.
Digest [S7] describes document drafting from approved text where a person still checks. Materials are not sent until the manager signs them.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. Public materials are checked against the fact rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends when the activities have been directed and only signed materials are sent. Booking income is out of scope.
Input contract: appeal id, fact id, approved sentence, audience, date. Producer is the manager from facts already signed. A line with no fact id is dropped.
The meeting prior fits the activities. Use the document store's own template before custom code. The send points at the signed version.
unknowns: Who may sign materials when the manager is away.
Which appeals are mail and which are events.
research_questions: What share of public lines has a fact id today?
How often is a draft line dropped at sign-off?

already_counted.description: Time directing fundraising stays with the manager

incremental.description: Update the materials template when a new appeal type starts

approvals.approved_version: fundraising materials signed for this appeal id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes appeal facts are not stored as rows, so materials are still rewritten by hand. The high case assumes the draft is clean but directing the activities and signing the text stay with the manager. Event time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Legislation notes and budget commentary are drafted from source rows. Media meetings, fundraising events and the signature on any public text stay with the manager.
reach: A finance colleague receives a budget pack whose commentary cites the figure rows.
Media contacts receive only the public text the manager has signed.
skills_to_grow: Read a proposed rule against the service list before advising what would change.
Administer a budget from figure rows, with commentary checked to those rows.
Send public and fundraising text only after a personal sign-off.
role.ambitious_version: A rule change and a budget version each have a signed note, and no public line goes out that the manager has not checked against the source rows.
